analysis:
This batch is documentation only: a new changelog (changelog.d/autopilot-placements-and-busy-reasons.md lines 1-9) and a 6-line addition to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head 351-356) about Autopilot placement holds. No source was supplied, so no regression can be shown from these units.

Claims that integration must verify against the provider source:
(1) Line 3: the Autopilot set expands to every downloaded, verified catalog build without a new consent step. Confirm verification uses the weight hash, not only the catalog ID (T-012, T-027, A-004).
(2) Line 4: coordinator-driven downloads are on by default. Check:
- the 50 GiB free-disk floor and the storage/model limits (T-016);
- that autopilot-downloads.json, kept beside the config, is owner-only and cannot be used by the operator to inject unverified models (TB-003).
(3) Line 5: adoption keeps serving after the control lease ends. Confirm adoption ends when:
- consent is revoked or Autopilot is disabled;
- the build fails verification;
- the provider restarts.
Also confirm adoption does not bypass publication, revision or authorization gates (T-052, T-053, A-016).
(4) Line 6 and hardware-support.md 351-355: holds of up to 24 hours exclude held slots from eviction and from reclaim credit. Check the availability impact: a coordinator-set hold could block ordinary loads (T-029-style DoS). The coordinator is trusted, so this is design behaviour, not a finding.
(5) Line 7: busy reasons and held/adopted models are now in heartbeats. This is minor metadata exposure to the coordinator only (T-058-adjacent).
(6) Line 8: the watchdog cancels stalled operations. Confirm cancellation releases pending-load claims.
(7) Line 9: new protocol fields are optional and coordinators that do not know them ignore them.

The threat model has no Autopilot or download entries, so it may need updating once the source is reviewed. I raised no findings because none is evidenced.
